claim_text: A seven-day survey of seven Xiamen WWTPs measured dissolved and adsorbed bisphenols; median BPA was 1318 ng/L in influent and 177 ng/L in effluent
source_title: Fate and mass balance of bisphenol analogues in wastewater treatment plants in Xiamen City China
applicability_boundary: Seven Xiamen municipal WWTPs; median not universal design concentration
notes: Supports BPA secondary-effluent admission and a 0.18 ug/L central scenario anchor

claim_text: In a municipal WWTP secondary effluent with background BPA about 0.45 ug/L dissolved organic matter reduced BPA solid-phase extraction and powdered-activated-carbon removal
source_title: Effects of dissolved organic matter on the efficiency of bisphenol A removal by adsorption and photocatalytic degradation
applicability_boundary: One Shincheon municipal WWTP secondary effluent in Daegu Korea
notes: DOM is a mechanistic competitor and analytical-recovery confounder

claim_text: Direct binding assays found BPA KD 5.50 nM for ERRgamma and analogue testing showed that one phenolic hydroxyl is sufficient while central-carbon substituent size and electronics affect binding
source_title: Direct evidence revealing structural elements essential for the high binding ability of bisphenol A to human estrogen-related receptor-gamma
locator: full text; saturation and analogue-binding sections
applicability_boundary: Protein mechanism reference only; not evidence that an artificial polymer reproduces the pocket
notes: Supports asymmetric single-anchor plus bridge-reading hypothesis; B-class unless paired with an actual natural sequestration process

claim_text: Nanopore confinement altered laccase-mediated degradation of BPA analogues but describes catalysis rather than reversible adsorption
source_title: Nanopores promote laccase degradation of bisphenol A and its analogues
applicability_boundary: Catalytic transformation study; cannot directly support adsorption capacity or reversibility
notes: Useful only for approach-corridor and phenoxyl-chemistry controls

claim_text: Across 148 Chinese municipal WWTPs the mean removal of total measured PFAS was -5.45 percent and no conventional process showed effective scavenging
source_title: Distribution source and ecological risk of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in Chinese municipal wastewater treatment plants
applicability_boundary: Fourteen measured PFAS and national Chinese WWTP sample; individual-panel distributions require supporting information
notes: Supports the class-level engineering gap but not identical risk across panel members

claim_text: In 44 Shaanxi WWTPs PFBA was dominant in influent and effluent and reached 11.4 ng/L in effluent
source_title: Occurrence fate and risk assessment of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in wastewater treatment plants in Shaanxi China
applicability_boundary: Shaanxi municipal WWTPs; maximum is not a central concentration
notes: Directly supports PFBA panel admission

claim_text: Functionalized PPN-6 materials tested PFBS PFPeA PFOA and PFOS at 250 nmol/L in wastewater; cationic ammonium PPNs narrowed the short-versus-long removal gap while wastewater competition remained measurable
source_title: Functionalized Porous Polymer Networks as High-Performance PFAS Adsorbents
journal_or_authority: Journal of the American Chemical Society
applicability_boundary: PPN platform and tested PFAS set; does not cover the full PFBS PFBA PFHxA GenX panel together
notes: Direct prior art against generic cationic plus hydrophobic porous polymers

claim_text: A 1.00 plus or minus 0.05 mmol/g IEC microphase-separated quaternized bead showed initial PFBA sorption 2.3 times that of whole Amberlite IRA 900 and complete desorption with 1 to 1 methanol and 1 M NaCl
source_title: Anion exchange beads for PFAS capture using a polymerization-induced microphase separation approach
locator: open full text; abstract and sorption sections
applicability_boundary: PFBA TFA and PFOA tests; ion-exchange resin identity excludes it as a main project contribution
notes: Mandatory state-of-the-art ion-exchange benchmark and prior-art attack

claim_text: A tunable porous beta-cyclodextrin platform showed that charge and cyclodextrin binding jointly control short- and long-chain anionic PFAS removal and that salt challenges the mechanism
source_title: A Tunable Porous beta-Cyclodextrin Polymer Platform to Understand and Improve Anionic PFAS Removal
locator: open article abstract and salt-response sections
applicability_boundary: Beta-CD PFAS polymer platform; exact performance depends on formulation and water matrix
notes: Direct prior art against unmodified cationic beta-CD concepts

claim_text: Infinite-dilution measurements separated hydrophobic and electrostatic contributions; weak-anion exchange affinity for PFBA was about 450-fold that of the tested HLB sorbent and the authors proposed sequential hydrophobic and electrostatic removal
source_title: Independent mode sorption of perfluoroalkyl acids by single and multiple adsorbents
applicability_boundary: Commercial analytical sorbents and unbranched PFAAs; not GenX or real secondary effluent
notes: Supports orthogonal-mode accounting and warns that apparent synergy may be additive

claim_text: Crosslinked bovine-serum-albumin-based adsorbents were tested against PFBS PFBA GenX and other PFAS and reached equilibrium within five minutes at 100 ug/L total test conditions
source_title: Rapid High-Capacity and Reusable Bovine Serum Albumin-Based Adsorbents for PFAS Removal
locator: publisher abstract and kinetics figure description
applicability_boundary: Protein adsorbent is outside project material scope; concentration and matrix are not the secondary-effluent main test
notes: May inform a nonprotein distributed-polar-pocket hypothesis but cannot be copied as material

claim_text: Swellable organosilica containing cationic and fluorous functions captured a 12-PFAS C4-C10 suite; cationic imidazolium polymer in expandable pores gave the highest reported capacity in that study
source_title: Absorption of short-chain to long-chain perfluoroalkyl substances using swellable organically modified silica
journal_or_authority: Environmental Science Water Research and Technology
applicability_boundary: Contains fluorinated groups and ion-exchange functionality; DI water and 50 mM NaCl rather than secondary effluent
notes: Direct prior against swellable mixed-mode pore claims and raises fluorinated-material lifecycle concerns

claim_text: A polyaniline silica surface-imprinted polymer reported selective adsorption of 2,6-DCP over related phenols and the non-imprinted polymer
source_title: Selective adsorption of 2,6-dichlorophenol by surface imprinted polymers using polyaniline silica gel composites
applicability_boundary: Aquatic laboratory study; environmental secondary-effluent relevance and trace-level performance not established
notes: Direct prior art; carrier-swapped 2,6-DCP imprinting is control-only

claim_text: The PoxR phenol-sensing domain structure with 2,4-DCP shows aromatic edge-to-face packing and accommodation of chlorine substituents in a hydrophobic pocket
source_title: Structural basis of phenolic effector recognition by the bacterial transcriptional regulator PoxR
applicability_boundary: 2,4-DCP complex and sensory protein; not 2,6-DCP adsorption or a material
notes: B-class geometry source for positional-isomer tests

claim_text: A phenol-bound structure of the DmpR ligand-binding domain resolved how a bacterial regulator recognizes phenolic effectors
source_title: Structural basis for effector recognition by the DmpR phenol-responsive transcriptional regulator
applicability_boundary: Phenol-bound sensor; exact 2,6-DCP affinity and water-matrix translation remain unproven
notes: Supports only a phenolic-pocket design constraint

claim_text: A purified chlorophenol 4-monooxygenase system was studied for degradation of mono- and dichlorophenols including 2,6-DCP
source_title: Characterization of a chlorophenol 4-monooxygenase system
applicability_boundary: Catalytic transformation is not reversible capture and cannot establish adsorption selectivity
notes: Can motivate an approach-channel hypothesis only if catalysis and irreversible oxidation are excluded

claim_text: Ralstonia eutropha JMP134 mineralized 2,6-DCP as part of a broad chlorophenol substrate range
source_title: Mineralization of chlorophenols by Ralstonia eutropha JMP134
applicability_boundary: Whole-cell biodegradation; broad substrate use and no isolated adsorption interface
notes: Biological handling exists but does not supply a selective adsorption hard correspondence

claim_text: A German PMT-vPvM screening compilation lists no wastewater-treatment-plant-effluent occurrence entry for 2,6-DCP and reports surface-water maxima around 27 ng/L
source_title: PMT vPvM assessment of REACH registered substances detected in wastewater treatment plant effluent freshwater resources and drinking water
applicability_boundary: Screening compilation; absence of an entry is not proof of absence
notes: Keeps municipal-secondary-effluent environmental admission unresolved

claim_text: An Australian wastewater report tabulated 2,6-DCP below a 10000 ng/L quantification limit in effluent; this LOQ is too high to establish trace occurrence or absence
source_title: Hazard characterisations of microplastics in wastewater
applicability_boundary: Non-detection at a high LOQ; not usable as an occurrence concentration
notes: Supports the evidence-gap disposition rather than admission

claim_text: Xanthomonas citri SsuA is required for growth on alkanesulfonates as sulfur sources; crystal structures with MES MOPS and HEPES show sulfonate oxygens coordinated by main-chain NH groups and polar residues in a spacious partly hydrated pocket
source_title: Structural and Physiological Analyses of the Alkanesulphonate-Binding Protein SsuA of the Citrus Pathogen Xanthomonas citri
locator: full text; ligand pocket and knockout-growth sections
applicability_boundary: Natural alkanesulfonate nutrient uptake; not direct PFBS binding
notes: A-class analogous natural function for sulfonate-head capture with a hydrated low-polarity pocket

claim_text: Bug-family periplasmic solute-binding proteins use two conserved beta-strand beta-turn alpha-helix motifs to form carboxylate pincers through direct and conserved-water hydrogen bonds; domain 1 anchors and domain 2 discriminates productive binding
source_title: Structure-based mechanism of ligand binding for periplasmic solute-binding protein of the Bug family
applicability_boundary: Natural carboxylate-solute transport; no PFBA PFHxA or GenX test
notes: Supporting analogous natural function for carboxylate-head capture and second-stage pocket discrimination

claim_text: TauA crystal structures and ITC with taurine and alkanesulfonates show conserved headgroup coordination but large affinity differences; simulations attribute specificity partly to different hydration states and desolvation penalties
source_title: Desolvation of the substrate-binding protein TauA dictates ligand specificity for the alkanesulfonate ABC importer TauABC
locator: open full text PMCID PMC6906117; ITC and hydration sections
applicability_boundary: TauA is taurine-preferring and does not establish PFAS affinity
notes: Direct warning that matching sulfonate geometry alone is insufficient and confined-water state must be measured

claim_text: Bis triethoxysilyl propyl urea can be co-condensed under CTAB-templated sol-gel conditions into urea-bridged mesoporous organosilica with 2.4 and 3.8 nm pores while retaining most Si-C bonds
source_title: Synthesis and characterization of urea bridged hybrid periodic mesoporous organosilica materials
applicability_boundary: Irregular particles and no PFAS adsorption test
notes: Establishes the exact neutral urea-bridge material family and pore-size feasibility

claim_text: Sequential delayed co-condensation can place organosilane functions throughout channels in selected channel regions or only on external surfaces depending on addition time
source_title: Selective Functionalization of the Outer and Inner Surfaces in Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles
applicability_boundary: Demonstrated on mesoporous silica nanoparticles; transfer to BTPU and phenylene PMO requires batch QC
notes: Manufacturing basis for a pore-mouth-enriched neutral pincer rather than a composition-only blend

claim_text: Alginate can act as a removable form-giving matrix for mechanically stable 2 mm silica and pure phenylene-bridged organosilica beads that retain mesoporosity after pseudomorphic transformation
source_title: Millimeter-sized micellar-templated silica beads and phenylene-bridged mesoporous organosilica beads
applicability_boundary: Phenylene PMO only; BTPU gradient adaptation is untested
notes: Supports recoverable fixed-bed form without permanent alginate binder mass

claim_text: A 2023 PMO platform with tunable fluoroalkyl and amine functions enhanced PFBA uptake; electrostatic interactions dominated while higher fluoroalkyl loading strengthened non-electrostatic contribution and the material treated PFAS mixtures in natural water
source_title: Enhanced adsorption of short-chain perfluorobutanoic acid by functionalized periodic mesoporous organosilica Performance and mechanisms
applicability_boundary: Fluorinated and amine-functionalized PMO; not neutral urea-phenylene spatial pincer
notes: Closest PMO prior and mandatory benchmark; generic PMO or mixed-function claims are not novel

claim_text: A cationic palladium metal-organic cage encapsulated PFBA PFBS PFHxA and other PFAS as anionic aggregates; log association constants remained at least 5 and 1 wt percent cage in mesoporous silica removed more than 98 percent under flow at 100 to 1000 ng/L
source_title: Efficient Removal of Short-Chain Perfluoroalkyl Substances by Cavity-Directed Aggregation in a Molecular Cage Host
applicability_boundary: Highly cationic Pd cage and custom host are outside project material scope; GenX not shown in abstract
notes: Strong direct prior for multiguest aggregation and trace flow performance; neutral nonmetal implementation must show a distinct causal gain

claim_text: A neutral microporous urea-functionalized POP used dense urea hydrogen-bond donors and a hydrophobic framework to recognize sulfonate and carboxylate dyes in water; a methyl POP deletion control adsorbed less
source_title: A neutral porous organic polymer host for the recognition of anionic dyes in water
applicability_boundary: Micromolar anionic dyes rather than trace PFAS; four-step monomer synthesis and Sonogashira POP
notes: Direct prior against claiming neutral urea plus hydrophobic pore itself as novel; spatial placement and PFAS-specific causality must carry the contribution

claim_text: Polyamide microplastics adsorbed PFBA PFHxA and longer PFCAs through pore filling hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen bonding but capacities were low and DOM sharply reduced uptake
source_title: Adsorption of perfluoroalkyl substances on polyamide microplastics Effect of sorbent and influence of environmental factors
applicability_boundary: 0.1 to 25 mg/L isotherms and environmental microplastic context; not a trace fixed-bed adsorbent
notes: Terminates commodity polyamide as a high-quality main route while retaining it as a low-cost mechanism control

claim_text: Among eleven syringe-filter materials nylon showed high PFAS loss; adsorption remained chain-length dependent and was mainly controlled by hydrophobicity electrostatics surface area and water chemistry although hydrogen bonding also contributed
source_title: Insights on the Adsorption of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances onto Laboratory Syringe Membrane Filters Experimental Materials and Mechanism Evaluations
applicability_boundary: Filter artifact study at elevated concentrations; panel included PFBS and GenX but not PFBA PFHxA
notes: Additional evidence that nylon uptake is not class-selective enough for the lead design

claim_text: Water encapsulated in activated-carbon pores increased adsorption capacities for PFHxA PFBS and PFBA by roughly 1.4 to 2.7 times relative to dry-reference activated carbon
source_title: Confined water-encapsulated activated carbon for enhanced adsorption of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
applicability_boundary: Activated-carbon platform and tested conditions; mechanism does not by itself establish class-over-EfOM selectivity
notes: Direct prior against a generic confined-water novelty claim

claim_text: A zeolite dynamic-hydroxyl-cycle material combined confined water clusters and framework interactions to remove short and ultra-short PFAS without requiring structure-specific binding for chains below C6
source_title: Dynamic hydroxyl cycle of zeolite for short and ultra-short chain PFAS free potable water
locator: open article abstract and mechanism description
applicability_boundary: Zeolite potable-water study; exact panel and secondary-effluent performance require full-data comparison
notes: Recent direct prior that crowds confined-water and framework-dual-binding claims

claim_text: EPA Method 1633A is a multi-laboratory-validated isotope-dilution LC-MS/MS method for 40 PFAS in aqueous matrices including wastewater and includes PFBA PFHxA PFBS and HFPO-DA
source_title: Method 1633A Analysis of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances PFAS in Aqueous Solid Biosolids and Tissue Samples by LC-MS/MS
applicability_boundary: Method implementation requires laboratory-specific MDL and full QC acceptance; not a material-performance source
notes: Binding analytical backbone for the E1 batch and column package

claim_text: A Western Australian multi-plant monitoring program measured sixteen phenols and detected eleven in secondary treated wastewater; 2,6-DCP was among five analytes detected in more than 30 percent of samples and its median differed significantly between KWRP and Beenyup WWTP
source_title: Perth Groundwater Replenishment Trial PCRP Chapters 6-9
journal_or_authority: Government of Western Australia Department of Health
locator: PDF pp 109-110; secondary wastewater phenols section and Figures 7-7 to 7-9
applicability_boundary: One authoritative regional program with multiple plants; exact numeric median is figure-based and this source alone does not satisfy the repository requirement for two independent sources
notes: Upgrades the DCP scenario from unsupported to conditional but does not close ENV-STOP

claim_text: In long-term activated-sludge culture EPS acted as a protective barrier and transferred 2,6-DCP from the liquid phase to sludge; batch distribution left 73 plus or minus 2 percent dissolved and about 26 percent sorbed
source_title: Distribution variation of a metabolic uncoupler 2,6-dichlorophenol in long-term sludge culture and their effects on sludge reduction and biological inhibition
locator: abstract plus methods and distribution section
applicability_boundary: Municipal sludge inoculum but synthetic wastewater and deliberately elevated 2,6-DCP; EPS attribution supports barrier organization rather than environmental concentration or positional selectivity
notes: Primary functional prototype for DCP20-01

claim_text: DHPB binds 2,6-DCP in a hydrophobic distal pocket and crystallography identifies binding positions different from those of 2,4-dihalophenols
source_title: Bridging the functional gap between reactivity and inhibition in dehaloperoxidase B from Amphitrite ornata Mechanistic and structural studies with 2,4- and 2,6-dihalophenols
locator: PDB 7M1I at 1.66 angstrom and article abstract
applicability_boundary: Catalytic globin structure is B-class support and cannot alone satisfy the biomimetic owner gate
notes: Direct target structural constraint for the DCP shallow cavity and positional-pose test

claim_text: A tetrachloroethene reductive dehalogenase structure contains 2,6-DCP in a highly apolar active site with the hydroxyl substituent oriented toward the cobamide center while substrate conversion proceeds by long-range electron transfer
source_title: Cobamide-mediated enzymatic reductive dehalogenation via long-range electron transfer
locator: PDB 5MA0 at 1.90 angstrom and article abstract
applicability_boundary: Catalytic enzyme and not an adsorbent; used only as an independent pose constraint
notes: Second direct target structure supporting one polar end and an apolar chlorine-accommodating cavity

claim_text: Tick olfactory sensilla are extraordinarily sensitive to 2,6-DCP but later structure-activity work found that 2,4-DCP can mimic it and that chlorine count rather than chlorine position dominates recognition
source_title: Structure activity studies of chlorophenol analogues as attractants for Rhipicephalus appendiculatus
applicability_boundary: Sensory response is not adsorption and does not support positional selectivity
notes: Negative evidence terminating tick-receptor geometry as the DCP main prototype

claim_text: A 2,6-DCP molecularly imprinted SERS material used MAA and acrylamide dual functional monomers in an aqueous detection workflow
source_title: High-sensitive molecularly imprinted sensor with multilayer nanocomposite for 2,6-dichlorophenol detection based on surface-enhanced Raman scattering
applicability_boundary: Analytical sensor with silica reduced graphene oxide gold and polydopamine rather than packed-bed secondary-effluent adsorbent
notes: Direct prior against claiming dual-monomer 2,6-DCP imprinting as novel

claim_text: BPA binds mainly to protein components of activated-sludge EPS by hydrophobic association and changes random-coil EPS into relatively condensed cores; neutral pH and higher ionic strength promoted binding
source_title: Insights into thermodynamic mechanisms driving bisphenol A binding to extracellular polymeric substances of activated sludge
locator: abstract and EPS extraction and formation sections
applicability_boundary: Extracted EPS from one WWTP and no component-deletion causality; supports condensed-microdomain organization but not BPA-specific selectivity
notes: Supporting process evidence for BPA spatial-domain designs and a warning against claiming specificity from hydrophobic condensation

claim_text: Aerobic activated sludge shows rapid BPA sorption followed by biodegradation with reported Koc values around 621 to 736 L per kg
source_title: Sorption and degradation of bisphenol A by aerobic activated sludge
applicability_boundary: Bulk partitioning is not a selective biological recognition mechanism
notes: Process reality support and negative control against overstating EPS specificity

claim_text: Tunable-fluorine COFs directly adsorbed BPA BPF and BPS and showed a nonmonotonic optimum in fluorination; reported mechanisms included pore filling pi stacking hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions
source_title: Tailored covalent organic frameworks with tunable fluorine groups for efficient adsorption of bisphenol analogues
applicability_boundary: Recent single-family bisphenol adsorption study and not evidence for BPA-selective reverse-logKow recognition in secondary effluent
notes: Crowds generic fluorinated COF and gate-tuning claims and demotes BPA20-03 and BPA20-20

claim_text: A TFPN crosslinked beta-cyclodextrin polymer adsorbed BPA among ten aqueous contaminants through hydrophilic and hydrophobic forces and investigated pH salts regeneration and reuse
source_title: Adsorption behavior and mechanism of aqueous organic contaminants on beta-cyclodextrin polymer
applicability_boundary: Broad organic-contaminant adsorption and no demonstrated BPA over close bisphenol analogues
notes: Recent direct prior confirming that bare beta-CD networks are engineering controls rather than BPA innovation

claim_text: A 2.20 angstrom HSA crystal structure contains two HFPO-DA molecules together with four myristates; solution work found lower affinity and stoichiometry than PFOA
source_title: Investigation of the Interaction between Human Serum Albumin and Branched Short-Chain Perfluoroalkyl Compounds
applicability_boundary: Ternary myristate context and two sites do not prove one transferable carboxylate ether branch cooperative pocket
notes: Direct occupancy fact and negative boundary for the terminated S3 mapping

claim_text: HFPO-DA in a Milan metropolitan WWTP outflow ranged from 2.5 to 72 ng/L with a reported mean of 35 plus or minus 31 ng/L; paired inflow was 59 to 79 ng/L
source_title: Impact of Wastewater Treatment Plant Discharge on Water Quality of a Heavily Urbanized River in Milan Metropolitan Area Traditional and Emerging Contaminant Analysis
applicability_boundary: One metropolitan study and substantial variability; not a universal design concentration
notes: Second independent municipal-secondary-effluent scenario source for HFPO-DA

claim_text: Commercial anion-exchange resins removed HFPO-DA and other perfluoroether acids from drinking and recycled waters; charge density controlled uptake and natural-water kinetics were pore-diffusion limited
source_title: Efficient removal of GenX HFPO-DA and other perfluorinated ether acids from drinking and recycled waters using anion exchange resins
applicability_boundary: Conventional ion exchange and not a biomimetic or GenX-selective mechanism
notes: Mandatory external benchmark and prior against permanent-charge novelty

claim_text: Quaternary-ammonium silica gel was compared with GAC for HFPO-DA in batch column and molecular simulation experiments and reported higher equilibrium capacity than GAC
source_title: Comparative study on Perfluoro 2-methyl-3-oxahexanoic acid removal by quaternary ammonium functionalized silica gel and granular activated carbon from batch and column experiments and molecular simulation-based interpretation
applicability_boundary: Quaternary silica is a conventional electrostatic and hydrophobic platform; trace secondary-effluent selectivity was not the biomimetic claim
notes: Direct GenX material benchmark for GX50-01

claim_text: A PFPE-modified polystyrenic ion-exchange sorbent captured eleven PFAS including HFPO-DA in salt and humic-acid backgrounds and in potable water and landfill leachate
source_title: Fluoropolymer sorbent for efficient and selective capturing of per- and polyfluorinated compounds
applicability_boundary: Fluorinated ion-exchange polymer is outside the preferred lifecycle and originality boundary
notes: Crowds combined fluorophilicity plus ion-exchange claims

claim_text: An amphipathic fluoroamine hydrogel removed a PFAS panel including GenX from real natural waters through combined fluorinated and cationic functions
source_title: Amphipathic fluoroamine-functionalized hydrogels for enhanced selective removal of anionic PFAS from water
applicability_boundary: Fluorinated cationic hydrogel and natural-water tests; not a nonfluorinated neutral packed-bed GenX geometry mechanism
notes: Recent direct prior and lifecycle exclusion control

claim_text: A molecularly imprinted polymer-modified microelectrode detected HFPO-DA in river water and included a nonimprinted control plus chloride humic acid and PFOS interferent tests
source_title: mu-MIP Molecularly Imprinted Polymer-Modified Microelectrodes for the Ultrasensitive Quantification of GenX HFPO-DA in River Water
applicability_boundary: Electrode sensor with direct GenX template rather than recoverable trace adsorbent; template background is a critical risk
notes: Direct prior against generic GenX imprinting novelty

claim_text: In 144 treated-sewage samples from Szczecin p,p-prime DDT had a reported mean of 0.05 plus or minus 0.07 ng/L a range of 0.04 to 0.28 ng/L and 79 percent detection; the summed DDT DDE DDD mean was about 0.16 ng/L
source_title: The Effect of Water and Sewage Treatment on Reducing Residues of Selected Organochlorine Pesticides in Szczecin Poland
applicability_boundary: One city and whole unfiltered solvent-preserved samples; phase distribution is not resolved
notes: Primary trace municipal-treated-effluent admission source for DDT family

claim_text: Two Hong Kong sewage treatment works had crude-sewage total DDTs near 6 ng/L and differed in treatment process removal and solid-liquid distribution
source_title: Profiles and removal efficiency of organochlorine pesticides with emphasis on DDTs and HCHs by two different sewage treatment works
locator: article abstract plus HKSAR technical-report phase data
applicability_boundary: Influent concentrations are clearer than final-effluent values in accessible metadata; treatment and phase evidence does not set a universal effluent concentration
notes: Independent WWTP source and reason to split whole filtered and particulate fractions

claim_text: DDT partition in egg phosphatidylcholine was about 260000; 50 mol percent cholesterol reduced it to about 120000 and lipid-chain length and phase transitions caused large nonmonotonic partition changes
source_title: Partition of DDT in synthetic and native membranes
applicability_boundary: Membrane partition is biological accumulation not wastewater adsorption and is not DDT-specific against all hydrophobes
notes: A-class functional prototype for chain-order and phase-dependent soft-domain partition

claim_text: Radiolabeled DDT left circulating chylomicrons and entered tissues faster than cholesterol ester and with a different tissue distribution
source_title: Tissue uptake of DDT is independent of chylomicron metabolism
applicability_boundary: Rat in-vivo transport and no molecular receptor; supports interfacial release rather than target-specific recognition
notes: Supporting functional prototype for a shallow accessible soft phase instead of bulk lipid capacity

claim_text: Virgin and regenerated activated carbon showed very strong sub-ng/L free-aqueous sorption of DDT DDE DDD and DDMU with log KAC values from 8.47 to 9.26
source_title: Sorption of dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane DDT and its metabolites by activated carbon in clean water and sediment slurries
applicability_boundary: Clean water and sediment-slurry remediation rather than secondary-effluent packed-bed polishing
notes: Mandatory high-affinity benchmark; new materials need matrix or regeneration value rather than pure-water capacity claims

claim_text: Noncovalent DDT imprinting in a BTEB sol-gel failed; sacrificial-spacer covalent imprinting with EDA or EBP produced selective DDT sensing films with a 50 ppt detection limit
source_title: Development and characterization of molecularly imprinted sol-gel materials for the selective detection of DDT
applicability_boundary: Sensor film and covalent-imprint chemistry rather than packed-bed family removal; proves weak noncovalent DDT imprinting is risky
notes: Direct prior and negative evidence governing LPO-SIP controls

claim_text: A magnetic MIP used a caffeic-acid choline-chloride formic-acid ternary DES functional monomer and a thymol-menthol DES dummy to recognize DDT DDE and DDD in produce
source_title: A magnetic molecularly imprinted polymer based on an eco-friendly deep eutectic solvent for the selective recognition of dichlorodiphenyl trichloroethane and its degradation products in fruits and vegetables
applicability_boundary: Analytical extraction from food with magnetic nanosorbent rather than secondary-effluent column treatment
notes: Direct family-wide dummy-imprint prior against broad novelty claims
